paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the same God who calls every star by name (Psalm 147:4) is the One who "heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds" (Psalm 147:3). Hold those two together. The One with understanding that "has no limit" (Psalm 147:5) is not too busy for your hurting heart. I've been tucked in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, when you feel forgotten, this verse is a warm cookie straight off the tray.

The psalm keeps showing that this God is great AND close. He covers the sky with clouds and makes grass grow on the hills (Psalm 147:8), and He feeds the young ravens when they call (Psalm 147:9). He is not impressed by "the strength of the horse" or "the legs of a man," but He is "pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion" (Psalm 147:10-11). So you don't have to be the fastest, the strongest or the most put together. You just hope in Him, and that's the whole recipe.

That's why this psalm opens with "Hallelujah!" and ends with "Hallelujah!" (Psalm 147:1, 20). It sings praise three times, and every time it gives reasons, because praise is the right answer to who He is and what He does. His word melts the frost and makes the waters flow (Psalm 147:18), so what can it do for a cold, heavy day of yours? Bring Him the broken parts, sing anyway, and let your praise be the first thing out of the oven.
